diagnosis.what_is_wrong: The trace does not establish a host or service fault explaining the reported slower coding task. It shows workload phases changing within one container, but the activity drop and later python3 work are not accompanied by evidence of host CPU saturation, disk/network degradation, or process restart; the sparse, partly unpaired scheduler-delay samples are not enough to attribute a slowdown.
diagnosis.evidence: Compared full-span activity from 01:57:57.900–01:58:30.800: sched_switch/wakeup and block events drop sharply around 01:58:03, then vary with workload; the late 01:58:15–01:58:29 interval has low scheduler/network/block counts while python3 consumes about 2.745 CPU-s over 01:58:14–01:58:26 (0.229 average cores). sched_stat_runtime shows 5.50055 CPU-s in pid_ns 4026531836 versus 0.00010 elsewhere, so there is no measured competing-container CPU surge. Process-life data shows claude and python3 throughout, with no coding-task restart. Raw scheduler records include some long claude wake-to-switch intervals, but most late paired samples are near-immediate and the early sample is only two pairs with nine new-thread wakeups unpaired; this is insufficient to establish starvation. Workers inspected scheduler, block, network, runtime, process-life, and raw event evidence; the trace lacks direct application task-duration evidence, so the operator-reported slowdown cannot be confirmed from this trace.
diagnosis.window_evidence: The full trace was checked, but no bounded interval has a defensible fault onset and recovery. The activity boundary near 01:58:03 and later low-rate period are workload transitions without corroborating resource-pressure evidence; 01:58:30 rebounds only in the final second and do not define recovery from a demonstrated incident.
